sections.overview: This highly localized Mexican cave salamander from Hidalgo is a lungless amphibian in family Plethodontidae.
sections.identification: Its webbed, spatulate toes and long tail help distinguish it from related Chiropterotriton salamanders.
sections.habitat: It is known from damp caves near Durango in Hidalgo, at about 2160 m in pine-oak country.
sections.diet: The sources reviewed do not report this species’ prey, so its diet remains unknown in species accounts.
sections.behavior: After 73 years without records, researchers rediscovered it inside a cave in September 2010.
sections.reproduction: The references provide no reliable species-specific details on courtship, egg laying or development.
sections.ecology: It shares a cave with C. magnipes; C. multidentatus was once considered a possible synonym, but taxonomy now separates them.
sections.conservation: An IUCN specialist-group profile lists it as Critically Endangered, citing its tiny range and cave-habitat concerns.
